title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 137
paragraphs: Whatever it is unlawful for them to do, it is also unlawful for them to speak of. The most disgraceful thing in their view is to tell a lie. The next most disgraceful is to owe a debt—for many reasons, but especially because they say a debtor is bound to tell lies. Any citizen with leprosy or a similar skin disease is not allowed to enter the city or mix with other Persians. They say such a person has sinned against the sun. Many Persians drive any foreigner with such a disease out of the country. They apply the same rule to white doves, for the same reason. They do not urinate or spit into rivers, nor do they wash their hands in them. They do not allow anyone else to do so either. They hold rivers in great reverence.
